body_markdown:
For data centre cooling teams, the point at which a refrigerant leak is detected can make a significant difference. Low-level leak detection can identify refrigerant loss at a much earlier stage, before significant refrigerant has been lost or cooling performance is affected.


As rack densities increase and cooling infrastructure works harder, small changes in system performance can matter. A low-level refrigerant leak may begin affecting cooling efficiency and place additional strain on equipment before there is an obvious failure or high-level alarm. This raises an important question: should leak detection only alert teams once refrigerant loss begins to affect system performance, or help identify low-level leaks much earlier?


**Moving beyond reactive maintenance**


A reactive approach typically begins with an alarm, followed by investigation, diagnosis and repair. Different monitoring technologies can provide different levels of early warning. Diffusion refrigerant monitors, such as the[MSA Bacharach® X30 and X50](https://gb.msasafety.com/xseries-refrigerant-monitors?locale=en) , are designed for occupant safety and typically have alarm thresholds set at around 150 ppm. By contrast, aspirated monitors, such as the[MSA Chillgard® 5000 Refrigerant Leak Monitor](https://gb.msasafety.com/p/000070000500001111?locale=en&default=1&regionIso=GB) and[Bacharach Multi-Zone Gas Monitor](https://gb.msasafety.com/p/000490000400001000?locale=en&default=1&regionIso=GB) , can detect refrigerant concentrations as low as 1 ppm, with alarm thresholds sometimes set higher, for example at 10 ppm, to help avoid excessive alarms. This low-level sensitivity can give maintenance teams an opportunity to investigate leaks before substantial refrigerant loss occurs.


By identifying low concentrations of refrigerant gas in the surrounding air, teams can investigate potential leaks before they develop into a larger cooling issue. This can support a more proactive maintenance strategy, where emerging problems can be addressed sooner and maintenance activity prioritised based on what is happening across the cooling system.


For mission-critical environments such as data centres, that additional visibility can be particularly valuable.


**High-precision monitoring across multiple zones**


The BACHARACH® Multi-Zone Refrigerant Gas Monitor detects very low concentrations of refrigerant in the air, which can indicate that a leak is present. It is designed for high-precision refrigerant detection using aspirated sampling. Rather than relying on individual sensors at each monitoring point, the monitor uses a central infrared sensor to sequentially monitor up to 16 zones. It can detect refrigerant concentrations as low as 1 ppm, helping teams identify low-level leaks that may otherwise develop unnoticed.


Sample lines can be positioned to monitor different zones across the cooling environment, depending on the layout and the areas requiring coverage. If refrigerant is detected in a monitored zone, maintenance teams can investigate potential leak sources in the surrounding equipment or units. Where more precise leak location is required, additional sample lines may be positioned near likely leak points, although a greater number of sampling points can increase installation costs.


For data centre applications, this can help provide earlier indication of refrigerant loss across cooling infrastructure and give maintenance teams more time to investigate before the issue becomes more significant.


**Extending visibility beyond the plant room**


Detection is only useful if the information reaches the people who need it. By connecting the BACHARACH® Multi-Zone Refrigerant Gas Monitor through ProtoNode and the[Parasense Enterprise Leak Detection (ELD)](https://gb.msasafety.com/p/ParasenseEnterprise?locale=en&default=1&regionIso=GB) cloud platform, refrigerant monitoring information can be accessed quickly and remotely.


This can give maintenance teams greater visibility of conditions across the cooling environment without needing to be physically present at the monitoring system. Alerts can also notify teams when low levels of refrigerant are detected, supporting faster investigation and helping teams prioritise where attention may be required.


For facilities operating multiple cooling systems, rooms or locations, this connected approach can make refrigerant monitoring easier to incorporate into wider maintenance activity rather than treating it as a standalone alarm system.


**Turning detection data into maintenance insight**


So, to sum up, the value of connected refrigerant monitoring is not simply knowing that a leak exists. It is having information early enough to make a more informed maintenance decision.


Combining high-precision detection through the BACHARACH® Multi-Zone Refrigerant Gas Monitor with the remote visibility provided by ProtoNode and Parasense ELD can help:


- Identify low-level refrigerant leaks earlier
- Monitor multiple areas from a central system
- Maintain remote visibility of refrigerant conditions
- Receive alerts when low levels of refrigerant are detected
- Investigate emerging issues before they develop further
- Prioritise maintenance activity based on available monitoring data


For data centres, the benefit is simple: earlier visibility creates more time to act. Bringing high-precision detection and remote monitoring into a connected strategy can help teams identify developing refrigerant leaks sooner, prioritise maintenance more effectively and reduce the risk of a minor leak escalating into a wider cooling issue.
